title: Burnell as soloist, speech impediment and improvising
summary: He was better solo than in a band, had a speech impediment, and played unnamed tunes of his own that changed each time.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: One time I had the idea he was mostly just a solo pianist, you know like playing by himself. Was he good in a band?

He was pretty good in a band but I mean he was better solo pianist by himself. He was not a good band man like Lester. See Lester was always a better band man than him, you know. He was a good band man. But just like you said, playing by himself, they couldn't touch him. They couldn't touch him, they couldn't do nothing. And I told you about when the barbers used to stand him up on the boxes, you know so he could reach the key. He was a small kid down here.
Yeah, he was playing for the small.

That's why I said if he was, if things was in them days like it was now, he'd have made I guess as much money as sugar child or more. Yeah if he got the record and television and everything else. Yeah and then he had a little tongue tie, a little impediment of speech like that.
Well I thought I was going to ask you if that was maybe due to a French accent or something. A lot of no. He was really tongue tied.

Yeah, yeah. He just talked like that. You know, couldn't talk to the, he said, talk to the, tell man where you doing, you know things like that. And then he tried to sing a little number sometime, you know. I mean if he'd record things like that he'd have been, oh he'd have been wonderful. I'm glad they'd really go for that. No.
Is there anything else you can think of to tell about Burnell if not there's a little something else?
No I don't think I'd tell no more about it.
You think he wrote many pieces or anything himself or just played other pieces? No, no, no.

I mean sometimes he'd sit by the piano and he'd say listen to this, he'd play something that you never heard before. You know something like that. Something you never heard before but he'd never, to my knowledge, never had no name for it or call it no special piece because the next time we play that same thing, he might put something else in it you know.
